# Record formats (kiln)

<!-- generated by tools/gen_formats_doc.py from schemas/*.schema.json; do not edit by hand -->

Every record kiln writes is a YAML or JSON file, or one line of a JSONL log, described by a JSON Schema
(draft 2020-12) in `schemas/`. A record's first key is `schema: "<repo>/<name>/<version>"`; a new
version always comes with a reader for the old one. Worked examples are in `schemas/examples/`. Read
records through the commands in [REGISTRY.md](../REGISTRY.md); never edit one by hand.

## caption-event

one image's training caption at one moment: One line of <home>/projects/<slug>/captions.jsonl: one caption per image; the latest line per image wins. Only `approved` captions are frozen or trained on. `source` is who wrote the text: operator, the second source, or a tool for drafts (for example kiln:captions propose).

- schema: `kiln/caption-event/1`
- file: [schemas/caption-event.schema.json](../../schemas/caption-event.schema.json)
- example: [schemas/examples/caption-event.example.json](../../schemas/examples/caption-event.example.json)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/caption-event/1` | yes | the format and its version; always the first key |
| `at` | string | yes | ISO 8601 time, for example 2030-01-01T00:00:00+00:00. New records always use T and carry the UTC offset; times exported from an older store may use a space and lack the offset. |
| `v` | `1` | yes | the line format's version: the number at the end of `schema`, so a reader can branch without parsing the string |
| `source` | string | yes | where the line's content comes from: `operator` (the person), the second source (policy.second_source_name, default `assistant`), or a tool, for example `kiln:images import` or `export:legacy` |
| `by` | string | no | the command that wrote the line, for example `kiln images label` (optional) |
| `image` | string | yes | an image id: img-<sha256[:12]> |
| `text` | string | yes |  |
| `word_count` | integer | yes |  |
| `status` | one of `draft`, `approved`, `rejected` | yes |  |
| `basis` | one of `prompt`, `manual`, `assistant`, `legacy` | no | what the text started from |
| `sheet` | string or null | no |  |
| `lint` | array of string | no | the lint findings when the line was written |
| `legacy_id` | string or integer or null | no | the record's id in the store it was exported from; null for records made here. Kept so a migrated record can be traced back; never shown in public text |

## config

kiln instance configuration (kiln.toml): The one TOML file at the instance root (<home>/kiln.toml). Found in this order: --workspace, $KILN_HOME, upward from the current folder, ~/.config/kiln/. Any key can be overridden with KILN_<SECTION>__<KEY>. `kiln config set <section.key> <value>` validates against this schema and refuses an unknown key or a wrong type (exit 2, file unchanged). Absolute paths belong only in an instance copy, never in a shipped file.

- schema: `kiln/config/1`
- file: [schemas/config.schema.json](../../schemas/config.schema.json)
- example: [schemas/examples/config.example.yaml](../../schemas/examples/config.example.yaml)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/config/1` | yes | the format and its version; always the first key |
| `instance` | object | no |  |
| `instance.name` | string | no | a short name for this instance |
| `instance.adopted` | boolean | no | true = an existing workspace the tool works beside through its own runner |
| `paths` | object | no | where the instance keeps its data. Relative paths are relative to the instance root; ${VAR} is expanded at load time. images_root (kiln, adopted projects only) is read-only until cutover |
| `paths.root` | string | no |  |
| `paths.models_root` | string | no | <models_root>: the folder that holds checkpoints/, loras/, ... |
| `paths.projects` | string | no |  |
| `paths.journal` | string | no |  |
| `paths.runtime` | string | no |  |
| `paths.images_root` | string | no | <images_root>: an existing dataset image folder that legacy members are copied from, read-only |
| `comfyui` | object | no |  |
| `comfyui.url` | string | no | the ComfyUI server's base URL; ComfyUI's upstream default is http://127.0.0.1:8188 |
| `comfyui.dir` | string | no | <comfyui_dir>: only when the tool starts and stops the server itself |
| `comfyui.python` | string | no | <comfyui_python>: that ComfyUI's interpreter |
| `comfyui.min_version` | string | no | the oldest ComfyUI version the graphs are tested with |
| `comfyui.manage_lifecycle` | boolean | no | true = the tool may start and stop the server |
| `comfyui.start_args` | array of string | no | extra arguments when the tool starts the server |
| `comfyui.timeout_s` | number | no | seconds to wait for one HTTP answer |
| `limits` | object | no | RAM needed per job comes from families/<f>.yaml host_ram_gb, not from here |
| `limits.host_ram_floor_gb` | number | no | free host RAM never given away to a job |
| `limits.disk_floor_gb` | number | no | free disk that a download or write must leave |
| `limits.max_concurrent_gpu_jobs` | integer | no |  |
| `limits.skip_ram_check` | boolean | no | true = start jobs without measuring free RAM (only where it cannot be measured) |
| `scheduler` | object | no |  |
| `scheduler.kind` | one of `none`, `command` | no | none = wait for free RAM and disk locally; command = call the *_command templates |
| `scheduler.fail_open` | boolean | no | true = run anyway when the scheduler cannot be reached (default false: fail closed) |
| `scheduler.poll_s` | number | no | seconds between checks while waiting |
| `scheduler.stop_file` | string | no | a file whose appearance asks a running job to yield |
| `scheduler.plan_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.ready_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.wait_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.start_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.check_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.requeue_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.done_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.cancel_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `scheduler.update_command` | string | no | a command template for this scheduler verb; written per machine, never shipped |
| `jobs` | object | no |  |

| `jobs.allowed[].tool` | one of `easel`, `kiln` | yes |  |
| `jobs.allowed[].verb` | string | yes |  |
| `jobs.allowed[].pausable` | boolean | yes |  |
| `review` | object | no |  |
| `review.bind` | string | no | address the review page listens on |
| `review.port` | integer | no |  |
| `policy` | object | no |  |
| `policy.reviewer` | one of `human-only`, `assistant-may-read-sfw` | no | who may look at images: only the person (default), or the assistant too for sfw images, its read labelled "assistant's read, not the verdict" |
| `policy.prompt_authoring` | one of `sfw-only`, `user-text-only` | no | sfw-only = the assistant may write sfw prompt text; user-text-only = only the person's words go into prompts |
| `policy.unknown_rating_is` | one of `nsfw` | no | unknown content is never treated as sfw |
| `policy.second_source_name` | string | no | the name verdicts and notes from the assistant are stored under |

Added 2026-11-06 before any release (additive, optional; no version bump). |

## coverage

the coverage board: <home>/projects/<slug>/coverage.yaml: what the dataset needs per dimension and bucket, not a raw image quota. Targets are the person's; `current` is refreshed by `kiln coverage board`.

- schema: `kiln/coverage/1`
- file: [schemas/coverage.schema.json](../../schemas/coverage.schema.json)
- example: [schemas/examples/coverage.example.yaml](../../schemas/examples/coverage.example.yaml)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/coverage/1` | yes | the format and its version; always the first key |
| `project` | string | yes | a project slug, for example demo_robot |
| `gaps` | array of object | yes |  |
| `gaps[].dimension` | string | yes | framing \| viewpoint \| expression \| outfit \| environment \| lighting \| category, or a project's own |
| `gaps[].bucket` | string | yes |  |
| `gaps[].target` | integer | yes |  |
| `gaps[].current` | integer | yes |  |
| `gaps[].priority` | one of `blocker`, `high`, `normal`, `low` | yes |  |
| `gaps[].status` | one of `open`, `filling`, `met`, `waived` | yes |  |
| `gaps[].note` | string or null | no |  |
| `gaps[].legacy_id` | string or integer or null | no | the record's id in the store it was exported from; null for records made here. Kept so a migrated record can be traced back; never shown in public text |

## decision-frontmatter

a decision's front matter: The YAML front matter of <home>/projects/<slug>/decisions/dec-NNNN.md (between the two `---` lines); the Markdown body below it carries the reasoning. Opened by `kiln decide open`, closed by `kiln decide`; only the person decides.

- schema: `kiln/decision-frontmatter/1`
- file: [schemas/decision-frontmatter.schema.json](../../schemas/decision-frontmatter.schema.json)
- example: [schemas/examples/decision-frontmatter.example.yaml](../../schemas/examples/decision-frontmatter.example.yaml)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/decision-frontmatter/1` | yes | the format and its version; always the first key |
| `id` | string | yes | a decision id: dec-NNNN |
| `legacy_id` | string or integer or null | no | the record's id in the store it was exported from; null for records made here. Kept so a migrated record can be traced back; never shown in public text |
| `project` | string | yes | a project slug, for example demo_robot |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `status` | one of `open`, `decided`, `superseded` | yes |  |
| `question` | string | yes |  |
| `options` | array of string | no |  |
| `decision` | string or null | no | the person's answer, verbatim |
| `rationale` | string or null | no |  |
| `supersedes` | string or null | no |  |
| `opened_at` | string | yes | ISO 8601 time, for example 2030-01-01T00:00:00+00:00. New records always use T and carry the UTC offset; times exported from an older store may use a space and lack the offset. |
| `decided_at` | string or null | no |  |
| `decided_by` | one of `operator`, `null` | no |  |

## eval-suite

a fixed evaluation suite: A suite of prompts and fixed seeds that every checkpoint of a run is rendered with. Shipped per LoRA type as types/<type>/eval_suite.yaml and copied into a project as evals/suites/<suite_id>.yaml; frozen once results exist (a change is a new version).

- schema: `kiln/eval-suite/1`
- file: [schemas/eval-suite.schema.json](../../schemas/eval-suite.schema.json)
- example: [schemas/examples/eval-suite.example.yaml](../../schemas/examples/eval-suite.example.yaml)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/eval-suite/1` | yes | the format and its version; always the first key |
| `suite_id` | string | yes | the file stem: lower case, digits, _ . -; the suite's own name within its project, without the project slug |
| `project` | string | no | a project slug, for example demo_robot |
| `legacy_id` | string or integer or null | no | the record's id in the store it was exported from; null for records made here. Kept so a migrated record can be traced back; never shown in public text |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `version` | string | yes | a dataset or suite version chosen by the person, for example 0.2.0 |
| `seeds` | array of integer | no |  |
| `seeds_per_prompt` | integer | no | how many seeds each prompt is rendered with, for a suite that fixes the count but not the seeds themselves |
| `prompt_assembly` | object | no | how the runner builds each prompt: template, who applies the trigger and the outfit, the negative |
| `prompt_assembly.<key>` | string | no |  |
| `inference` | object | no | fixed render settings, flat or one block per family group; the family's defaults when absent |
| `inference.sampler` | string | no |  |
| `inference.scheduler` | string | no |  |
| `inference.steps` | integer | no |  |
| `inference.cfg` | number | no |  |
| `inference.width` | integer | no |  |
| `inference.height` | integer | no |  |
| `inference.clip_skip` | integer or null | no |  |
| `inference.negative` | string | no |  |
| `inference.shift` | number or null | no |  |
| `columns` | array of string | no | what is rendered per prompt and seed: checkpoint steps plus controls such as base or no-trigger |
| `prompts` | array of object | yes |  |
| `prompts[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `prompts[].category` | string | yes |  |
| `prompts[].text` | string | yes |  |
| `prompts[].stress_case` | string or null | no |  |
| `prompts[].framing` | one of `close`, `medium`, `full`, `wide`, `null` | no |  |
| `frozen_at` | string or null | no |  |
| `notes` | string or null | no |  |

## family

model family (kiln): One model family per file, families/<id>.yaml. The shared keys (all but `schema` and the tool block) are identical in the easel and kiln copies; `sync_common.py --check` compares them. A family with `inherits` reads the blocks it leaves out from its parent, except `licence_summary` and `host_ram_gb`, which every file carries.

- schema: `kiln/family/1`
- file: [schemas/family.schema.json](../../schemas/family.schema.json)
- example: [schemas/examples/family.example.yaml](../../schemas/examples/family.example.yaml)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/family/1` | yes | the format and its version; always the first key |
| `id` | string | yes | equals the file stem |
| `name` | string | yes | display name |
| `status` | one of `tested`, `experimental`, `unverified`, `listed` | yes | tested = trained or rendered with on the reference machine; experimental = run once, not in the tested path; unverified = priors only; listed = known, no recipe |
| `inherits` | string or null | yes | the parent family; a block this file leaves out is read from the parent (deep merge, the child's keys win) |
| `architecture` | object | no |  |
| `architecture.kind` | string | yes | for example unet-sdxl, dit-flux; unknown when not known |
| `architecture.latent_channels` | integer or null | yes |  |
| `architecture.text_encoders` | array of string or null | yes |  |
| `architecture.native_resolution` | integer or null | yes | the side length in pixels the family was trained at |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `licence_summary` | object | yes | the base model's licence in one line; every family carries its own, inherited or not (families check fails otherwise). It is the fallback for foundation bases only: a resource's own licence block wins |
| `licence_summary.status` | one of `verified`, `unverified`, `unknown` | yes |  |
| `licence_summary.name` | string or null | yes | the licence's name, null when not recorded |
| `licence_summary.text` | string | yes | one line a person can act on, for example 'unverified: read the model card' |
| `licence_summary.url` | string or null | yes | the model card; null is allowed (families check warns) |
| `licence_summary.spdx` | string or null | no |  |
| `licence_summary.checked_at` | string or null | no |  |
| `host_ram_gb` | object | yes | what the scheduler waits for before it starts a job of this family |
| `host_ram_gb.train` | number or null | yes | free host RAM a training step needs |
| `host_ram_gb.eval` | number or null | yes | free host RAM an eval render needs |
| `host_ram_gb.eval_includes_comfyui_server` | boolean or null | yes | true = the eval number already covers the ComfyUI server |
| `host_ram_gb.basis` | string | yes | measured on the reference machine, inherited, or a prior; say which |
| `training` | object | no | kiln's training recipe for this family |
| `training.supported` | boolean | yes | false = kiln has no tested training path for this family yet |
| `training.basis` | string | no |  |
| `training.note` | string | no |  |
| `training.trainer` | object | no |  |
| `training.trainer.name` | string | no |  |
| `training.trainer.version` | string | no |  |
| `training.trainer.commit` | string | no |  |
| `training.network` | object | no |  |
| `training.network.module` | string | no |  |
| `training.network.dim` | integer | no |  |
| `training.network.alpha` | number | no |  |
| `training.network.train_unet_only` | boolean | no |  |
| `training.optimizer` | object | no |  |
| `training.optimizer.type` | string | no |  |

| `training.optimizer.learning_rate` | number | no |  |

## feedback-event

triage and release feedback: One line of <home>/projects/<slug>/review/feedback.jsonl. Dataset triage: kind score (a verdict and checklist marks on one image), role (an anchor role set, added, removed or cleared), pair (which of two images is the better reference), note. After a release: kind release (feedback on a published version, entered by hand; comments are never fetched automatically). Captions go to captions.jsonl, not here.

- schema: `kiln/feedback-event/1`
- file: [schemas/feedback-event.schema.json](../../schemas/feedback-event.schema.json)

Each line is the image's complete record after `event`; the latest line per id wins. `root` + `file` locate the bytes (root images = the read-only images_root; imports = projects/<slug>/images; legacy_output = a host's render folder). Images are never opened for content: hash, size and dimensions only.

## materialized

a materialised dataset folder's record: <home>/projects/<slug>/datasets/<version>/_meta/materialized-<version>.json, written by `kiln dataset materialize`. Same nine keys as the record the older tooling writes (plus `schema`), so its readers keep working. record_sha256_12 = the first 12 hex digits of sha256 over this object without record_sha256_12, serialised with Python's json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) (default separators).

| `snapshot_manifest_sha256` | string | yes | lower-case hex sha256 of the file bytes |
| `materialized_at` | string | yes | ISO 8601 time, for example 2030-01-01T00:00:00+00:00. New records always use T and carry the UTC offset; times exported from an older store may use a space and lack the offset. |

| `items[].review.hint` | string | yes |  |
| `items[].example` | string | yes | the item filled in for the synthetic demo subject |
| `review_only` | array of object | yes |  |
| `review_only[].key` | string | yes |  |
| `review_only[].label` | string | yes |  |
| `review_only[].hint` | string | yes |  |
| `review_only[].skip_when` | object | no |  |
| `review_only[].skip_when.viewpoint` | array of one of `front`, `front_three_quarter`, `profile`, `back`, `rear_three_quarter`, `unusual` | no |  |
| `review_only[].skip_when.framing` | array of one of `close`, `medium`, `full`, `wide` | no |  |
| `review_only[].when` | string | no | the intake answer that switches the check on, for example `mouth = never_teeth` |

## type-dataset-toml

kiln LoRA type: dataset.toml: The dataset template of a LoRA type (types/<id>/dataset.toml) for kohya-ss sd-scripts. The file uses exactly the variables listed in `x-kiln-variables`; `kiln types check` replaces each with its sample value, parses the result as TOML and validates it against this schema. The `kiln` table is read by kiln (network rank, alpha, learning rate become trainer flags) and removed before the copy reaches sd-scripts, whose dataset config accepts only `general` and `datasets`.

- schema: `urn:kiln:type-dataset-toml:1`
- file: [schemas/type-dataset-toml.schema.json](../../schemas/type-dataset-toml.schema.json)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kiln` | object | yes |  |
| `kiln.network` | object | yes |  |
| `kiln.network.rank` | integer | yes |  |
| `kiln.network.alpha` | number | yes |  |
| `kiln.network.learning_rate` | number | yes |  |
| `general` | object | yes |  |
| `general.caption_extension` | `.txt` | yes |  |
| `general.keep_tokens` | integer | yes |  |
| `general.shuffle_caption` | boolean | yes |  |
| `general.caption_dropout_rate` | number | yes |  |
| `general.enable_bucket` | boolean | yes |  |
| `general.min_bucket_reso` | integer | no |  |
| `general.max_bucket_reso` | integer | no |  |
| `general.bucket_reso_steps` | integer | no |  |
| `general.flip_aug` | boolean | yes |  |
| `datasets` | array of object | yes |  |
| `datasets[].resolution` | array of integer | yes |  |
| `datasets[].batch_size` | integer | yes |  |
| `datasets[].num_repeats` | integer | no |  |
| `datasets[].validation_split` | number | no |  |
| `datasets[].validation_seed` | integer | no |  |
| `datasets[].subsets` | array of object | yes |  |
| `datasets[].subsets[].image_dir` | string | yes |  |

## type-intake

kiln LoRA type: intake.yaml: The intake questionnaire of a LoRA type (types/<id>/intake.yaml): 14 numbered questions, each with a default and an example answer for the synthetic demo subject. `kiln project new` copies it into a project; the person fills every `answer`. Checked by `kiln types check`.

- schema: `kiln/type-intake/1`
- file: [schemas/type-intake.schema.json](../../schemas/type-intake.schema.json)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/type-intake/1` | yes |  |
| `type` | string | yes | the type id; equals the folder name |
| `version` | integer | yes |  |
| `about` | string | no | one paragraph for the person who fills the intake |
| `policy` | object | yes |  |
| `policy.subjects` | `fictional-adults-only` | yes |  |
| `policy.refusal` | string | yes | the sentence kiln prints when it refuses a subject |
| `not_asked` | array of object | no |  |
| `not_asked[].topic` | string | yes |  |
| `not_asked[].default` | string or number or boolean or array of any or object or null | yes |  |
| `not_asked[].note` | string | no |  |
| `questions` | array of object | yes |  |
| `questions[].n` | integer | yes |  |
| `questions[].id` | string | yes |  |
| `questions[].question` | string | yes |  |
| `questions[].you_give` | string | yes | what the person answers with |
| `questions[].drafts` | string or null | no | what an assistant may draft from the answer, for the person's approval; never the answer itself |
| `questions[].choices` | array of string | no |  |
| `questions[].default` | string or number or boolean or array of any or null | yes | used when the answer stays null; null means there is no default |
| `questions[].required` | boolean | yes | true: kiln refuses to scaffold while the answer is null |
| `questions[].applies` | boolean | no | false: the question does not apply to this type; `default` explains what is used instead |
| `questions[].feeds` | array of string | yes | the files and fields the answer ends up in |
| `questions[].note` | string | no |  |
| `questions[].example` | string or number or boolean or array of any or null | yes | an answer for the synthetic demo subject; never a default |
| `questions[].answer` | string or number or boolean or array of any or null | yes | the person's answer; null in the shipped type |

## type-thresholds

kiln LoRA type: thresholds.yaml: The starting thresholds of a LoRA type (types/<id>/thresholds.yaml), grouped by stage. Every number is a dated prior from earlier work, not a law: the file says `validate on your subject first`, and a project changes a value only with a dated note and a decision. Checked by `kiln types check`.

- schema: `kiln/type-thresholds/1`
- file: [schemas/type-thresholds.schema.json](../../schemas/type-thresholds.schema.json)

| field | type | required | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `kiln/type-thresholds/1` | yes |  |
| `type` | string | yes |  |
| `dated` | string | yes | the day these priors were written down |
| `status` | `validate on your subject first` | yes |  |
| `basis` | string | yes |  |
| `change_rule` | string | no |  |
| `groups` | object | yes |  |
| `groups.<key>` | object | no |  |
